items.title: FAA Tech Upgrade Update, Trump Asia Agenda, Petition To Reinstate Huang At Nvidia
items.summary: Another technology problem disrupted United Airlines flights on Monday night as President Trump pushes Congress for more money to modernize the nation’s air traffic control system and Democrats question how previously approved funds are being spent. Trump is in Asia for a historic summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, after the White House said Ukraine would be off the agenda and Trump later said he plans to discuss it. Silicon Valley leaders are rallying around ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, as pressure grows on the company’s board to reconsider his resignation while questions about the scandal and Nvidia’s future remain unresolved.
items.body: Another technology problem disrupted United Airlines flights on Monday night as President Trump pushes Congress for more money to modernize the nation’s air traffic control system and Democrats question how previously approved funds are being spent.

items.title: FAA Ground Stop Update, Democratic Leadership Contest, Trump's Travels To Asia
items.summary: Airlines are recovering from a nationwide ground stop caused by a failure during routine FAA maintenance, raising new questions about the aging air traffic control system just ahead of the Thanksgiving travel rush. Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen is challenging Chuck Schumer to lead Senate Democrats, arguing the party’s midterm wins should not mean a return to business as usual. President Trump heads to Asia for meetings with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, where the White House says he plans to focus on nuclear weapons while leaving Ukraine and tensions over artificial intelligence off the agenda.

items.title: Russia-bound ship still on fire after attack in Gulf of Finland
items.summary: Finnish defence forces say that Ukraine was likely behind the drone attack on the vessel.
items.body: Rescue and firefighting efforts are continuing for a Russian cargo vessel hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland, authorities have said. The ship - the Sparta II - was bound for Russia's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad when it was hit on Saturday morning, before drifting into Finnish waters.

items.title: Italian jeweller and businessman Paolo Bulgari dies aged 89
items.summary: In a statement to Italian media, his family remember him as "the greatest jeweller of our time".
items.body: Italian jeweller Paolo Bulgari, who helped turn his family's business into a global luxury brand, has died in Rome aged age 89. His family announced the news, remembering him as "the greatest jeweller of our time", according to Italian media.

items.title: FBI reportedly investigating apparent hack of its criminal database
items.summary: The National Crime Information Center database is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information.
items.body: The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its criminal information database, US media reports, citing two people briefed on the issue. The National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database is used by federal and local law enforcement to share information on warrants and background checks.

items.title: Bank of England directors illegally profited from post-abolition enslavement in Cuba
items.summary: New research finds that the British-led Cobre Mining Company helped industrialise Manchester via copper deposits and enslaved African people • Slave-trade wealth was embedded in Britain’s financial system, research finds British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research. Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba, which supplied British firms during the Industrial Revolution, the historian Chris Evans has found.
items.body: British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.

items.title: NFL legend John Madden’s unlikely, unfiltered brilliance: ‘Coach was indeed animated’
items.summary: With the release of a new David O Russell biopic about the coach turned commentator turned gaming icon, those who knew him best remember his singular career Wearing his Oakland Raiders uniform and helmet, and gripping an orange traffic cone like a lance, Ted Hendricks rode into the training session on a roan horse and stopped at the 50-yard line. Some American football coaches might have reacted to the stunt with fury. But John Madden was unfazed. “We needed some relief from the intense grind,” recalls Hendricks, 79, who had borrowed the horse from a nearby stable. “It was a spur of the moment idea, but put a smile on everyone’s face. All Coach said once I dismounted was, ‘All right guys, Ted’s here, let’s get started.’ But I know he got a kick out of it too – just from the look on his face and the comments he made later in interviews.”

items.title: It will soon be too late to regulate use of autonomous weapons, warns Red Cross
items.summary: Warning about putting ‘genie back in the bottle’ comes as UN conference fails to agree on regulation instrument The International Committee of the Red Cross and rights groups have warned that it will soon be too late to put the “genie back in the bottle” as the development of autonomous weapons appears to outpace efforts to regulate them. The stark warning came as more than 120 member states of the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons concluded a week-long conference in Geneva.
items.body: The International Committee of the Red Cross and rights groups have warned that it will soon be too late to put the “genie back in the bottle” as the development of autonomous weapons appears to outpace efforts to regulate them.

items.title: Spuds in space: scientists say potatoes could be key food source for future moon base
items.summary: New report details how potatoes were successfully cultivated in simulated lunar soil The humble potato could be the key to sustaining human life on the moon , according to a new scientific report asserting that prolonged lunar exploration will depend on life support systems capable of producing food there. Potatoes are an ideal candidate for farming on the moon, scientists on a project backed by the US space agency Nasa concluded, after they succeeded in growing them in simulated lunar soil.
items.body: The humble potato could be the key to sustaining human life on the moon, according to a new scientific report asserting that prolonged lunar exploration will depend on life support systems capable of producing food there.

items.summary: 2022 — A shooting at a Walmart in Chesapeake, Virginia leaves seven workers dead, including the shooter, and four others injured.
items.body:
2022 — A shooting at a Walmart in Chesapeake, Virginia leaves seven workers dead, including the shooter, and four others injured.

2014 — While playing with a toy gun in Cleveland, 12-year-old African American Tamir Rice is killed by a white police officer.

2010 — During the Cambodian water festival, a stampede in Koh Pich, Phnom Penh, kills 347 people.

2004 — The Orange Revolution begins in Ukraine, resulting from the presidential elections.

2003 — Baghdad DHL attempted shootdown incident: Shortly after takeoff, a DHL Express cargo plane is struck on the left wing by a surface-to-air missile and forced to land.
